elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: The redline expressly preserves a Customer-payable liquidated amount: "the sole liquidated amount payable by PB upon any termination shall be a single early-termination fee not exceeding three (3) months of fees under this Agreement". A preferred (no-LD) result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula; here the Section 14.2 formulas (300% of Development Costs; Development Costs plus 25% per annum) also remain on the page.  The drafter targeted the fallback, so the preferred level is intentionally unmet.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: New 14.4.2 states the "sole liquidated amount payable by PB upon any termination shall be a single early-termination fee ... in lieu of the amounts specified in Section 14.2 and of any claim for damages", and the sentence retains the opening "Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary" override, so the 14.2 amounts are expressly displaced as the liquidated recovery. (Note the residual drafting risk flagged in reasons: the retained 14.2 sentences still recite payment obligations framed as consideration for the Trial Data Package.)

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is expressed as "three (3) months of fees under this Agreement", but this Agreement contains no periodic "fees" concept — the payment architecture is Development Costs, Approval Payments, Buy-Out Payments and the SFJ Interim/Final Management Fee. The cap therefore rests on an undefined measure and yields no ascertainable amount; the ceiling must be re-anchored to a defined base (e.g. "three (3) months of the SFJ Interim Management Fee" or a stated dollar figure).

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Operative text: "the sole liquidated amount payable by PB upon any termination shall be a single early-termination fee", stated in lieu of the Section 14.2 amounts and of SFJ's damages claim. Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments and Section 6.4 default interest are elective/ordinary payment mechanics rather than liquidated amounts, so they do not displace this element.

reasons: Fallback is incomplete on the cap element: "three (3) months of fees under this Agreement" uses an undefined trigger. The Agreement defines Development Costs, Approval Payments, Buy-Out Payments and the SFJ Interim/Final Management Fee, but never a monthly "fee". Repair by anchoring the ceiling to a defined base or a fixed dollar cap (e.g. "an amount not exceeding three (3) times the monthly SFJ Interim Management Fee then in effect").

Intent fails on retained contradictory language and dangling mechanics. Sections 14.2.1, 14.2.2 and 14.2.10 still say PB "will pay SFJ ... an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs" / "Development Costs ... plus interest at the annual rate of twenty-five percent (25%)" expressly "in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results ... as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4". Because those sums are characterised as purchase consideration rather than damages, SFJ can argue they survive a proviso that speaks only to the "sole liquidated amount". Add an express conforming cut-back in 14.2 (or state that the early-termination fee is the sole amount payable on termination, whether as damages or as consideration for the Trial Data Package).

Further dangling cross-references: 14.2.2 and 14.2.10 still reduce future Approval Payments "by the amount previously paid by PB to SFJ pursuant to this Section 14.2.2 / 14.2.10", an offset that becomes meaningless once the 14.2 amounts are displaced; and 14.2.2's Trial Data Package transfer under Section 11.1.1.4 would proceed with its stated consideration removed. Conform those offsets and the Section 11.1.1.4 purchase mechanic.

Minimality is satisfied: the edit is confined to the 14.4.2 exclusive-remedy proviso, retains the favourable "without prejudice to other remedies" and in-lieu-of-damages language, adds no survival tail, expense, procedure or extra remedy, and leaves Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments and Section 6.4 default interest untouched.

Classification as a deviation is correct: a Customer-payable formula of 300% of Development Costs (and Development Costs plus 25% per annum on a mere JSC disagreement) sits at or beyond walk-away territory, well outside the three-months cap.
